small_guidance:
- The GEMM (1024×8192×8192 fp32) dominates runtime; the LSE+activation kernel is negligible. Tuning BLOCK_N/num_warps in the epilogue kernel won't move the needle. If staying small, try a 2D grid epilogue with BLOCK_N=2048 and num_warps=8, but expect <1% gain.
- For the epilogue, you can drop num_stages to 1 (single-pass online LSE, no pipelining benefit) and increase BLOCK_N to 2048 to halve loop iterations.
- The real lever is the cuBLAS `F.linear`. Verify cuBLAS is using TF32 (it is fp32 input on Ada, no TF32 by default for fp32 matmul unless `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=True`). Enabling TF32 in `__init__` could give a large speedup with the loose 5e-2 tolerance.
large_guidance:
- Replace `F.linear` with a custom Triton GEMM that fuses the LogSumExp reduction directly into the matmul epilogue: tile across M (rows) and stream over N (out_features) with BLOCK_N as the reduction-fusion axis. Each program owns a row-block, accumulates GEMM tiles into a row of size out_features in registers/SMEM only long enough to feed an online LSE running-max/running-sum, never materializing the 1024×8192 output. This eliminates an 8192×8192 weight read for the epilogue pass and removes the intermediate write/read of gemm_out (~256MB).
- Alternatively, do a split-K GEMM where each program computes a partial dot product for one (row, out_col) and write to gemm_out, then a second kernel does online LSE — but the fused producer-reduction is strictly better for memory traffic.
- Enable TF32 (`torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=True`) globally in ModelNew init; the 5e-2 tolerance easily accommodates it and cuBLAS fp32-GEMM on Ada with TF32 is ~4-8× faster than IEEE fp32.
